name: vision_explain_bad
title: The same explainability report with seven planted defects
origin: domain-vision round 2: the dirty twin of vision_explain. Its MLV114 label is the positive control for VIS2-01 - the identical defect that a workspace Dataset subclass hides fires here, because the dataset is a torchvision ImageFolder

expected.defect: clean_accuracy() no longer calls model.eval(), and load_model() no longer returns an eval-mode model
expected.why: every BatchNorm in the ResNet-50 trunk updates its running statistics from the test split while the headline accuracy is being measured, so the number reported and the weights that produced it are not the same model
expected.note: found at 0.59 / possible, below mlview.minConfidence 0.6: the architecture is a torchvision resnet50 whose layers MLView cannot resolve, so the documented de-rate applies

expected.why: the autograd graph for a ResNet-50 over the whole test split is built and dropped

expected.defect: the evaluation pipeline gained RandomResizedCrop and RandomHorizontalFlip
expected.why: every number in the report - clean, TTA, FGSM, PGD and both calibration errors - is measured on a different random view of the test set, so the report is not reproducible and is systematically pessimistic
expected.note: found twice, once per evaluation loader, at 0.58 / possible - below the Problems-panel threshold

expected.why: the eight Grad-CAM overlays written at the end of the run are a different eight images every time, so two runs cannot be compared image by image

expected.defect: torch.load with neither map_location= nor weights_only=True
expected.why: a downloaded checkpoint executes whatever its pickle says to execute, and a CUDA-saved checkpoint will not load on a CPU machine

expected.defect: the temperature is fitted on the test logits and the calibration error is then reported on the same split
expected.why: eceAfter is a training score presented as a held-out one; the whole point of calibration is that the scalar is fitted on data the reported number does not come from
expected.gap: MLV102 is the direct analogue - a transformer fitted on the test split - but it is written for sklearn FIT/FIT_TRANSFORM roles on a knowledge-table transformer. A torch nn.Module with a .fit() method that consumes a TEST_SPLIT-tagged value is the same defect and no rule models it.

expected.defect: the same augmented eval pipeline, reported a second time for the second evaluation loader
expected.why: MLView emits one MLV114 per evaluation loader the pipeline reaches; the second is the same defect seen from the test loader rather than the validation one, so it is neither a new hit nor a false positive

forbidden.why: unchanged from the clean twin, and it still fires: nothing encloses TemperatureScaler.fit in a no_grad region. Round-2 finding VIS2-12
unchanged from the clean twin, and it still fires: tta_accuracy calls model.eval() at line 101 and tta_logits calls it again at explain.py:112. Round-2 finding VIS2-13
there is no sklearn transformer in this project
there is no training loader in this project - nothing trains
the loaders are built inside build_loaders(), reached only from main() under the __main__ guard
the only optimizer is an LBFGS whose closure zeroes first, and LBFGS is the documented skip
GradCAM, fgsm and pgd back-propagate to produce a map or a perturbation, not to update parameters
the LBFGS closure protocol is zero_grad -> backward -> return, stepped by optimizer.step(closure)
every accumulator reduces with .item() or runs under no_grad
robust_accuracy still has no decorator on purpose - FGSM and PGD need the gradient with respect to the input - and the part that needs no graph is still wrapped in `with torch.no_grad():`
every accuracy is still computed after argmax(dim=1)
the softmax in tta_logits never reaches a cross-entropy
there is no sigmoid and no BCE loss in this project
load_model still moves the model with .to(device) and every batch is moved inside every loop
there is no split in this project - val/ and test/ are separate directories
there is no plain list or dict of submodules anywhere

gaps.what: no rule models a torch module with a .fit() method consuming the test split - the torch analogue of MLV102, and the standard shape for post-hoc calibration, prototype classifiers and kNN heads
gaps.evidence: report.py:132 against the clean twin's fit(val_logits, val_labels)
